sm: The hosts discuss the cases of missing and dead scientists. The guest says the disappearances do not seem random, and focuses on Amy Eskridge, who founded the Institute for Exotic Science and worked on exotic propulsion. She claimed that people from the future, from two warring factions, were warning that bunkers were needed. She also said a beam burned her hands as she typed. Both speakers note that she was vocal that she would never take her own life, yet she was found dead, and that some people dismiss her as kooky. They then discuss her dislike of Hal Puthoff, who never mentions the time traveler story on podcasts. They suggest that disclosure about UFOs is being released slowly, starting with the 2017 New York Times report, and that time travel is too strange a place to begin.

The conversation moves to other cases. They recommend the American Alchemy YouTube channel, then discuss Joshua LeBlanc, an electrical engineer who worked on NASA nuclear propulsion instrumentation. He left his phone and wallet at home, visited the Huntsville airport, and then drove his Tesla into rural Mississippi, where it burned. They also mention Anthony Chavez, an HVAC worker who left his wallet and cigarettes. One theory is that people are being targeted because they know of a breakthrough. The guest reads text messages from Eskridge to Samuel Reed of Geometric Sciences Corporation. In them she says she was surveilled after writing a note about Bob Lazar's story and element 115. She believed a private defense contractor, not the government, was behind the threats. They connect this to Havana syndrome and say people threatened by energy breakthroughs could be in danger.
